newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds stable, unaffected by reform debate.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds stable, unaffected by reform debate.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed stable with a positive trend on Monday and were unaffected by a rift between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor on a proposed capital market reform, traders said.
* CPI (consumer price index) linked government bonds: unchanged at 167.77
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 166.23
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct 157.98

"In the meantime there are no signs the market has been affected positively or negatively (by a decision to postpone a vote on a key part of the reform). The market is waiting for an announcement on September's CPI tomorrow," Israel Discount Bank investment adviser Gila Shkury said.

Israel's cabinet adopted early Monday morning only part of the Finance Ministry's proposal for capital market reform, postponing a decision on a politically sensitive tax on short-term savings that was a key component of the proposed reform.
The cabinet's marathon debate which started on Sunday revealed a rift between Netanyahu, who opposes the tax, and Meridor.
September's CPI will be published on Tuesday and economists estimate it will post a rise of 0.5 to 0.6 percent against a 0.4 percent increase in August.
"What is influencing the market is a lack of supply of CPI-linked bonds, which is pushing prices up," Shkury said.

The lack of supply is because the government has practically stopped issuing these bonds in favour of unlinked bonds and because investors are holding on to these bonds in expectation of a devaluation of the shekel, she said.

"Trading was quiet today with slight price rises," said financial consultant Eliezer Carmel. "The market seemed to be totally indifferent to cabinet debate on the reforms and the feeling is that decisions have yet to be made."

"One of the big problems afflicting the capital market is a lack of public faith that Netanyahu will be able to implement the economic reforms he has said he will undertake. The feeling is there is no leadership that can solve the economy's problems," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
